question: Why did Gandhi suspend the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Occurrence of Chauri Chaura incident**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Non-Cooperation Movement was suspended by Gandhi in February 1922 after the violent Chauri Chaura incident in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• On February 4, 1922, a clash between protesters and police led to the mob setting a police station ablaze, killing 22 policemen.
 
• Gandhi believed in non-violence as the core philosophy of the movement, and the Chauri Chaura incident contradicted this principle.
 
• He feared that the continuation of the movement might lead to more violent outbreaks and derail the original purpose of achieving independence through peaceful means.
 
• The suspension of the movement showcased Gandhi’s commitment to his principle of non-violence even at the cost of halting the struggle for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **British promises of reforms**

 
 
• During the Non-Cooperation Movement, the British government attempted to pacify Indians by promising minor reforms under the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act 1919).
 
• However, these reforms were widely criticized for being inadequate and incapable of fulfilling the aspirations of Indians for self-governance.
 
• These promises did not play a direct role in Gandhi’s decision to suspend the movement.
 
 
 
• **Arrest of national leaders**
 
 
• The British administration arrested several leaders during the Non-Cooperation Movement to suppress the agitation.
 
• However, the arrests were a regular part of the colonial government’s strategy and did not directly impact Gandhi’s decision to halt the movement.
 
• The arrest of Gandhi himself occurred later, in March 1922, after the suspension of the movement.
 
 
 
• **Failure of Khilafat support**
 
 
• The Khilafat Movement, which aimed to protect the Ottoman Caliphate, was supported by Gandhi to unite Hindus and Muslims in the struggle against British rule.
 
• While the Khilafat Movement eventually lost momentum due to changes in Turkey and waning enthusiasm, this was not the immediate cause of suspending the Non-Cooperation Movement.
 
• Gandhi’s decision was primarily driven by the Chauri Chaura incident, not the failure of Khilafat support.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Non-Cooperation Movement**
 
 
• The Non-Cooperation Movement, launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, was a mass protest against British colonial rule.
 
• It involved boycotting British goods, institutions, and titles while promoting swadeshi products and indigenous education.
 
• The movement marked a significant phase in India’s struggle for independence, showcasing Gandhi’s leadership and the power of mass mobilization.
